item: One robots entry, one schedule stamp and one politeness interval per host, whatever userinfo a URL carries; the userinfo masked in the activity monitor and in the URL logs outside the fetcher (R621)
summary: R621, OPEN_QUEUE item 46 (the leftovers R620 named), three parts in one PR. (1) ONE ENTRY PER HOST. The fetcher keyed every per-host record by scheme://netloc and netloc WITH the URL's userinfo (src/ingest/__init__.py, fetch() and declared_sitemaps()), so http://alice:pw@host/a and http://host/b were two hosts. Measured with the real EthicalFetcher against a 127.0.0.1 server: two robots.txt reads, the first sending the credentials as Basic auth (the robots URL was built from that key); two entries in robots_cache.json and in host_schedule.json, the user name and password written to disk; two politeness intervals (_last_request); two per-host locks; and two Tor circuits, the stream-isolation SOCKS user name being the netloc with its punctuation taken out, so the password reached the proxy. Now one helper, _host_netloc (the netloc after its LAST @, exactly the host and port urllib.parse reads), keys all of them: the robots decision, cause and failure count, the schedule stamp, the interval, the lock and the circuit, and the two readers crawl_delay_for and forget_robots. The two persistence-failure DEBUG lines and the clock-corrected-stamp INFO line therefore name the host only (fixed by the key, not by masking the lines). The robots.txt request goes to the page URL's scheme, host and port, without the credentials: one anonymous read per host is what one entry per host means, and a host whose robots.txt itself needs the credentials now answers 401 and is refused (fail-closed, as for any crawler without them). The page request is unchanged and still sends them. A backslash before the @ (urlparse and urllib3 read two hosts) used to be refused at the robots read as robots_unavailable (unreachable, cached under the hostile key); its robots read is now the anonymous one of the urlparse host, the host the SSRF guard checks, and the page is refused as BlockedTarget. (1b) AT LOAD an older build's credentialed keys leave both files and memory. robots_cache.json's are DROPPED: an entry is a cache whose absence costs one robots.txt read, and a decision read WITH the credentials is not the anonymous answer the host's one entry holds. host_schedule.json's are MERGED into the host's: a stamp is the host's own stated wish and lapses by time alone, so the later not_before and the larger delay_s win. The file is rewritten at construction only when it holds one (atomic, under its lock, best-effort); the four loaders leave them out even if that rewrite failed, and the two writers never carry one forward. (2) ActivityMonitor.fetch_started kept the raw URL and its netloc. The URL is served by /api/system/vitals as current_fetch.url and last_url, and the top bar shows _shortUrl(current_fetch.url), which strips only the scheme and www. (app-core.js); the host is the task manager's per-source rates row (per_host_rates, read by app-core.js _renderVitals) and inflight_hosts. Both now come from failure_url(url) (https://***@host/x and ***@host); no UI script needed a change, and the host read never raises. (3) The URL log lines outside the fetcher write the URL through failure_url, imported on use because a top-level import would load src.ingest into every keyword pass (the services package loads duckduckgo.py): duckduckgo.py fifteen (redirect unwrap unparseable, no target, target not http(s); URL validation; non-http(s) scheme; domain extraction; ethical fetch refused; discovered N feeds; valid feed found; unexpected discovery error; URL resolve failed, path and base; feed validation refused; feed validation error; found feed for a domain), url_utils.py three (canonicalize, domain, base URL), security.py two (sanitize_url, safe_href), link_analyzer/extractor.py four (relative URL and its base, malformed link, normalise). Tests: tests/test_host_key_userinfo_r621.py, 33 cases (the loopback server and an in-memory session; one robots entry, one stamp, one interval, one lock and one circuit for both URLs; the robots read's host, port and missing Authorization header, and the page's kept one; declared_sitemaps, crawl_delay_for and forget_robots; the three log lines; an older build's files dropped and merged at load, in the loaders alone and in the writers; the monitor directly and through the fetcher; every log site with caplog; a fresh-interpreter probe that the four modules do not load src.ingest; and controls: an ordinary URL keeps its keys, its log text and its monitor slots, and a file without a credentialed key is not rewritten). On the base 8e1f59a28, 24 fail and the 9 controls pass. tests/test_failure_url_sites_r620.py's robots-unavailable case now expects the bare host in 'robots.txt for <scheme://host> could not be determined' for a credentialed URL (R620 expected ***@ there; the key now holds none). 48 mutants, all killed: each key site raw, _host_netloc the identity, each load-time scrub, loader filter and writer filter removed, the merge made a drop or the earlier stamp or the smaller delay, the drop keeping the keys, each monitor slot raw and its guard removed, each of the 24 log sites raw, and a top-level import. Not changed, named: data handed back to a caller rather than logged (duckduckgo _extract_domain returns the netloc with its userinfo as a result's domain; url_utils.canonicalize_url keeps it in Article.canonical_url, beside Article.url, which stores the URL as given; the link records keep an article's links as written); an exception's own text (urllib.parse's NFKC netloc check names the netloc with its userinfo, and log_failure writes that line by design); _guarded_redirect_get's circuit fallback, reached only by the two preflights, which build their URLs from a source's domain; and a host fetched with and without credentials in one window shows two per-source rate rows (***@host and host), the mask kept as ruled. Found and left: api/jobs _live_fetch passes the snapshot's current_fetch dict to urlparse, so the job label is always 'fetch in flight'. Release-notes line: a web address that carries a user name and password is now treated as the same site as the address without them, so that site's robots.txt and crawl delay govern both, its robots.txt is read without those credentials, and they are no longer written into the app's politeness caches, the activity indicator, the task manager or the logs.
